newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen rising moderately after US rally.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen rising moderately after US rally.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to post moderate gains on Wednesday, as a surge on Wall Street on Tuesday will ease concern among Tokyo traders over U.S. stocks' fragility and encourage them to try higher levels in Tokyo, brokers said.
On Monday, the key 225-share Nikkei average closed up 57.51 points or 0.31 percent at 18,670.37. June Nikkei futures gained 20 points to end at 18,650. Tuesday was a market holiday.
"The U.S. stock surge has erased one unclear factor," said Seiki Orimi, manager of stock information services at Dai-Ichi Securities Co Ltd.
But brokers also said market participants were unwilling to take on large positions ahead of the coming three-day weekend. They expect the Nikkei 225 to edge higher to around 18,800.
The market is expected to see an influx of new money from pension funds, who have bought stocks actively since the fiscal year started on April 1, brokers said.
"High-techs and raw material issues are likely to lead the market, backed by the weak yen," Orimi said.
On Tuesday, the Dow industrials unofficially closed up 179 points, or 2.65 percent, at 6,962. It was the blue-chip index's second-largest point rise in a single day.
U.S. stocks rocketed higher as weaker-than-expected data on wage inflation and orders for manufactured goods soothed Wall Street's concerns over rising interest rates.
There had been fears in Tokyo that strong U.S. economic data might hit the Dow this week, brokers said.
